subject: Urgent: VertexX experiencing p95/p99 spikes on hosted API (32k flows)
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@vertexx.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency + errors on hosted API - 32k flows

Ben,

We started seeing sharp p95/p99 increases on our production flows this morning and it's impacting user-facing features. Key observations from our dashboards (last 24h):
- p95: 240ms -> 620ms (median steady)
- p99: 420ms -> 1.85s (major regressions corresponding to long-context requests)
- error rate: 0.23% -> 1.9% (503s / timeouts marked by our client)
- spike appears correlated with requests that send ~32k token contexts (indexing + long prompt inference).

Examples: request IDs included in attached trace_20270509.zip. Latency spikes started roughly 07:30 PDT and we've seen 10+ user-impacting incidents since then. This is on your hosted API (us-west region).

We need immediate mitigation and a timeline: if we can't get p99 under 1s or a clear mitigation path within 12-24 hours we'll have to route our latency-critical endpoints to a fallback provider. That would be very disruptive — we want to avoid it.

Can you escalate this with your engineering and infra teams and share an emergency plan?

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Director, ML Platform
VertexX

Immediate asks from our side to help triage (if you can provide quickly):

- sample payloads (anonymized is fine) — attach as text if possible

Short-term mitigations we're going to try while we investigate:
- enable tenant-level prefix caching for VertexX to reduce repeated KV work
- temporarily constrain max_context for your latency-critical route to 16k (opt-in)
- apply conservative per-tenant admission control to smooth bursts

I'll set up a war room if necessary. Laura — can you help coordinate an emergency call and share availability?

Ben

Thanks — triaging now. Quick notes from initial log sweep (us-west pools serving rwd-llama-32k-v2):
- Several nodes show elevated slow-path execution where kernel selection fell back to generic kernels for long sequence lengths; associated CPU spin observed in request worker threads (likely due to memory fragmentation + quantization path mismatches).
- KV cache churn: a handful of tenants with large context footprints are evicting large prefix entries; this increases compute per request and exacerbates tail latency.
- We see increased GC/allocator stalls on some nodes while JIT/compilation caches are repopulated after restarts.

Immediate mitigations I can enact in the next 1–2 hours (with approval):
- Enable stronger prefix-level caching for VertexX (reduces repeated KV decoding for identical prefixes).
- Pin VertexX traffic to a pool with more headroom (spin 4 gpus as a warm dedicated pool) — I can allocate warm nodes immediately; exact ETA ~45–90m to be warm.
- Deploy a temporary admission-controller throttle to cap concurrent long-context requests per tenant (smoothing bursts).
- Backport a small change to prevent synchronous compilation fallback for 32k paths (risk: small increase in memory usage; rollout: canary to 5% of requests).

I need: the specific failing request IDs and a couple of full payloads to reproduce locally (attachments). If VertexX can agree, we can also temporarily trim their max_context for latency-critical endpoints to 16k and route heavy indexing to an async batch path. That would likely bring p99 down quickly while we stabilize the runtime.

I'll open JIRA INF-1942 and attach traces. Laura — please confirm you have authority to approve emergency warm pool spend (we'll estimate 4 GPU-hours).

- Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

[internal reference: JIRA INF-1942]

1) Temporarily set your latency-critical route to max_context=16k (we can make it tenant-configurable; this is reversible).
2) Enable aggressive prefix caching for your tenant immediately.
3) Spin up a 4x GPU warm pool (us-west) for 12 hours to absorb burst traffic while the runtime fix is validated. Estimate ~4 GPU-hours of emergency capacity; we'll credit/cap costs as part of this incident resolution.

We also request 3 failing request IDs and two anonymized payloads so engineering can reproduce. You can drop them into the attached plain text file or paste into the thread.

If you approve, we can start the changes now (we expect p99 to drop materially within 30–90 minutes after caching + pool warm-up; full stabilization after the admission controller and any small runtime backport).

Thanks — Ben
